svg.title: Flower Anatomy Drag & Drop - Educational Interface
svg.desc: Static SVG educational tool for learning flower anatomy. Use the word bank to match labels to parts. Buttons open popups via internal anchors and CSS :target.

g.text: WORD BANK — Drag labels to the correct slots

text.tspan: 1. Study the flower diagram on the left.
2. Drag the labels from the word bank
below to the correct empty slots.
3. Use the arrows as guides for each part.

g.text: Pollination enables seed production and plant reproduction.
petal: Brightly colored to attract pollinators
sepal: Leaf-like structures that protect the bud
stamen: Male part made of filament + anther
pistil: Female part: stigma + style + ovary
anther: Produces and holds pollen grains
filament: Slender stalk that holds the anther
ovary: Base of pistil that contains ovules
style: Tube that connects stigma to ovary
stigma: Sticky top that receives pollen
receptacle: Swollen base that holds all parts
Tip: Match the words in the bank to the empty slots using the arrows as guides.
Great job! All parts correctly identified.
The interface has been reset to its initial state.
All slots are now empty and ready for new attempts.
In a real interactive tool, labels would return to the word bank.

svg.text: This is a static educational simulation. Click the buttons above to reveal hints and answers. No data is saved.
